sec-cover.html:
- Welcome. This session is Elastic Security: where we start, what changed in the landscape, and what we are announcing today.
- The graphic is the platform: Elasticsearch underneath, Security and Observability as solutions, and the services the agents use: Workflows, Kibana, the context engine, Jina AI models and Streams.
- Say "Elasticsearch" or "one platform" out loud. Do not use the retired platform brand name.
sec-platform.html:
- For everyone here from search or observability, half a minute on what Elastic Security is, before anything new.
- (SIEM builds) It is a SIEM: every security signal in Elasticsearch, at retention, and ES|QL to ask it precisely.
- (Elastic Defend builds) It is endpoint security: Elastic Defend, our own agent on the host. It prevents, responds and ships the data.
- (Native automation builds) And it is native automation: workflows and agents built in, not a separate SOAR to buy.
- (Bar lands) Nothing here is stitched to the side of the platform. We still do the job you buy us for.
- Land: "every agent you'll meet today stands on this platform."
- On the slide, Automatic Migration says "from your legacy SIEM". Name the source SIEMs out loud if you want to.
sec-numbers.html:
- And the job gets done.
- (2,000+ counts up) Two thousand open detection rules on GitHub, free to read, run and change.
- (Bars rise) One hundred percent, seven times over: AV-Comparatives has scored our endpoint perfect in five straight test cycles, and this month we were the only vendor with a hundred percent on both active and passive response.
- (Bar shrinks) Our own security team now triages an alert in under three minutes, thirty by hand before, because agents do the investigating first.
- (Strip) Forrester and IDC call the SIEM a Leader.
- Say "malware protection" if you elaborate on the 100% run, not "everything": Real-World H1 2026 was 99.8%.
- Sources: own count of github.com/elastic/detection-rules, Sep 2026. AV-Comparatives Business Security Tests Mar 2025 to Jun 2026 and EPR Test 2026. Triage figure: Elastic Security Labs, Jul 2, 2026 (Customer Zero, self-reported). Forrester and IDC wording needs the firms' usage approval.
sec-attackers.html:
- Last year on this stage the story was the rise of adversarial AI. This year every trend line landed.
- Walk the four rows top to bottom as one argument: attackers crossed human parity in social engineering, then a state actor let an agent run most of an intrusion, then AI became the median attacker's standard toolkit, and then in July an agent swarm ran an entire intrusion by itself.
- Defensive AI stopped being a preference somewhere on this slide. The July row is deliberately last: it is the rest of the talk.
- The slide face carries no vendor names. Sources to cite out loud: Mar 2025, Hoxhunt (hoxhunt.com/blog/ai-powered-phishing-vs-humans). Nov 2025, Anthropic (anthropic.com/research/disrupting-AI-espionage). May 2026, Verizon 2026 DBIR, AI research with Anthropic (verizon.com/dbir). Jul 2026, Hugging Face, OpenAI, METR and Redwood Research, Aug 26.
- Check the Hugging Face specifics against the public record before stage, and never imply they are an Elastic customer.
sec-signals.html:
- You all watched the same incident this month: swarms of agents, collaborating, colluding, moving at machine speed.
- (Dots fire) Here is the uncomfortable part, as reported: everything they did was detectable.
- (Connections fail) Most of it probably was detected. Nobody joined the signals into one campaign.
- Land: "never seen as one". Then, as the bridge: "imagination, in a SOC, is a query, and you can only ask it of all your data, in one place, continuously."
- The face carries no company name, dates, counts or outcomes by design. Verify specifics against Mike Nichols's deck before saying them, and say "as reported".
sec-siem.html:
- Before our story, the landscape. Attacks now come from new vectors, at machine speed, and they propagate through your environment at machine speed.
- (Signals converge) The old way of seeing across signal types, one tool at a time, does not work at that speed.
- (Questions appear, one per card) Where do you go to see the human and non-human identities in your environment? Where do you go to see lateral movement? Where do you find the devices compromised by swarms of agents nobody knew existed?
- The answer is the SIEM. All of your data, in one place, where agents can work on it. That is the fulcrum.
- Land: "help us use it".
sec-journey.html:
- Look at what three years produced.
- 2023: we put a language model next to the analyst, Elastic AI Assistant for Security. It made a good analyst faster.
- 2024: Attack Discovery, hundreds of alerts in, a handful of narrated attacks out. Automatic Import: a sample log in, a finished integration out.
- 2025: Automatic Migration moves a whole SIEM onto Elastic. The Elastic Inference Service keeps models on our side of the wall.
- 2026: agents with tools. Agent Builder with skills, Elastic Workflows, the MCP app, and the automated alert analysis flow.
- Three of these have patents pending.
- Land: "Each one did a whole job. The gap was never capability. It was connection."
sec-alert-zero.html:
- Earlier this year we gave that idea a name: Alert Zero. The SOC's inbox zero. Watch what it does to a queue.
- (Build) Security Alert Analysis classifies every alert, true positive, false positive or inconclusive, with reasoning. Flip the optional switch and high-confidence noise closes itself.
- What survives goes to Attack Discovery, which hunts raw events, checks entity risk and corroborates before it calls anything an attack.
- Embed it in Workflows. Let it draft the rules that close gaps, with a human approving.
- And here is the limit: it works one lane, the alert queue, and it waits for a person to press the button. Teams asked us: why does it wait for me?
sec-never-waited.html:
- So we asked the obvious question. What if it never waited? And what if every lane ran this way, all day: the hunts, the rule tuning, the investigations, the response actions?
- (Flood) Same night. Everything that landed after ten p.m.: every alert, the overnight hunts, the rule that needed an exception, the investigation nobody had opened, the response actions waiting for an owner.
- (Collapse) Most closed as noise, each with its reason written down. The rest folded into what they actually were: one attacker, one stolen credential, one decision.
- Your analyst sits down at eight-thirty to the evidence, the recommendation, and a button that still needs a human.
- The volumes are illustrative. Say so once if you quote the number.
sec-introducing.html:
- Today, in Elastic Security: it does now.
- (Name lands) And the agentic layer that does the running has a name: AlertZero. Pause two full seconds after the name.
- AlertZero runs the SOC. It works every alert, closes the noise, fixes the rules, acts on the real ones, and hunts for what nothing fired on. Continuously. With a human on the loop.
- (Cards) Four Watches, each with one job: Triage, Detection, Hunt, Forensics. Every finding lands in one shared Investigation.
- Never say "is now a fully agentic": we were agentic before. AlertZero makes the platform run the whole SOC.
sec-alertzero-platform.html:
- (Elasticsearch rises) Start at the bottom, because that is where the agents start. Elasticsearch, all your data, at retention. ES|QL, one query language across clusters, projects and external sources you never ingested. The Context Engine remembers what the Watches learned and what you decided.
- (Tiles) On that, everything Elastic Security already is. Nothing here is new to you.
- (Band) On top, AlertZero. Four Watches. Configured once, here. The layer directs; the platform executes.
- (Team row) Above all of it, your team. Every finding is an evidence-backed Proposal. You approve or reject.
- Land: "Built in, not bolted on."
- Compliance: "Context Engine" is an internal term with no public claim behind it. If it is not cleared, rename the card. External federated sources are experimental: no GA implication.
sec-watch.html:
- So what is a Watch? A named team of agents with one job, on duty around the clock, reporting to your people.
- Triage Watch works every alert. Hunt Watch hunts continuously and says so when it finds nothing. Detection Watch fixes the rules, not the symptoms. Forensics Watch is specialist depth when a case needs it.
- (Settings slide into place) You set how far each one goes: Manual, Assisted or Supervised, per Watch.
- Land: "Watches take the shifts nobody could staff, and your people keep every seat that decides."
- Autonomy level names are working names.
sec-autonomy.html:
- And you set how far the platform goes, per Watch.
- Manual: it surfaces the attack with context and a suggestion. You initiate, you approve every step. That's the default.
- Assisted: the investigation runs on its own and you get a finished assessment. Closing and response still wait for you.
- Supervised: approved classes finish end to end inside boundaries you set, and you're told afterwards, with the reasoning and an undo.
- You configure this once, at the AlertZero level; the components inherit it.
- Then the demo hand-off: "Enough slides. Let me show you the platform running."
sec-demo.html:
- Hold this slide while you switch the projector to the live build.
- The same theft, twice: two hosts, one stolen credential, one attacker who did their homework. Six beats, about ten minutes, on the real build, including the moment it finds nothing.
- Do not say "MCP App" on stage during the demo; it is out of scope for this talk.
